comment: Injection grammar for Mark (.mk.md) generic directives on top of VS Code's bundled markdown grammar (text.html.markdown). See docs/format.md for the three directive forms (container :::name{...}, leaf ::name{...}, inline :name[label]{attrs}) and the shared {...} attribute-block grammar, and docs/scripting.md for the fence-meta {name=...} group. Scope names are conventional TextMate scopes suffixed .markii so stock themes color them without extra configuration.

attribute-pair.comment: key=value in any of the three forms: key="double quoted", key='single quoted', key=bare. Quoted values may contain escaped quotes; bare values run until whitespace or a brace.

attribute-flag.comment: A bare flag attribute (no `=value`), e.g. `collapsed` or `publish`. Only tried where attribute-pair did not already match, since attribute-pair is listed first.
attribute-flag.name: entity.other.attribute-name.markii

attributes-block.comment: The {...} attribute block shared by all three directive forms (docs/format.md). Defined once and included wherever a directive may carry attributes.
attributes-block.name: meta.directive.attributes.markii

directive-label.comment: The optional [label] shared by all three directive forms.
directive-label.name: meta.directive.label.markii

directive-container-open.comment: Opening line of a container directive: three or more colons at line start, then a name, then optional [label] and {attrs}. docs/format.md's :::callout{type=warning title="Careful"} form.
directive-container-open.name: meta.directive.container.markii

directive-container-close.comment: Closing line of a container directive: three or more colons at line start and nothing else.
directive-container-close.name: meta.directive.container.markii

directive-leaf.comment: A leaf directive standing on its own line: exactly two colons at line start, then a name, then optional [label] and {attrs}. docs/format.md's ::stat{data=stars label="GitHub stars"} form. Regex specificity keeps this from ever matching the opening line of a container: the third literal colon required by directive-container-open is not a letter, so '::' followed by ':' never satisfies this pattern's '[A-Za-z]' requirement.
directive-leaf.name: meta.directive.leaf.markii

directive-inline.comment: An inline directive anywhere in a line: :name[label]{attrs}. docs/format.md's :kbd[Ctrl+S] / :badge[beta]{color=purple} form — and also the label-less :badge{color=purple} form, since a directive's [label] is optional (docs/format.md: 'a name, an optional [label], and optional {attributes}'). The lookahead requires either the [label] bracket or the {attrs} brace to follow immediately (per the generic-directives grammar this format is built on) — that is also what keeps a bare ':' in prose from ever being treated as a directive: a name with neither bracket after it never matches. The negative lookbehind additionally guards against matching the ':' inside a URL scheme like https://example.com, since that colon is preceded by a word character.
directive-inline.name: meta.directive.inline.markii

fence-meta-attributes.comment: The {name=...} fence-meta group after a code fence's language word (docs/scripting.md, e.g. a lua-tagged fence with a {name=stars} meta group). Trade-off, read before touching this rule: VS Code's bundled markdown grammar has its own rule for the whole fence line (backticks + language + this meta group) that begins matching at column 0, and the tokenizer always prefers whichever candidate starts earliest in the line, so this injected rule — whose earliest possible start is at the '{' — can never win on a real fence line; the built-in fenced_code.block.language.attributes.markdown scope wins there instead, and that is the correct, accepted outcome (losing this highlight is far cheaper than risking the alternative). Do NOT reach for a wider lookbehind to try to anchor this to the actual fence line: Oniguruma (vscode-oniguruma, what VS Code tokenizes with) only accepts FIXED-width lookbehind, or an alternation of fixed-width branches — 'bounded' quantifiers like {3,6} or {1,20} are still variable-width and raise ONIG_ERR_INVALID_LOOK_BEHIND_PATTERN at grammar-compile time, which would break tokenization for every markdown file opened, not just fail quietly. So instead this rule uses a one-character fixed-width lookbehind (a preceding space/tab) plus a content requirement — a lookahead demanding a name= or src= key inside the braces (docs/scripting.md: only a block carrying name= or src= is runnable) — to keep it from claiming arbitrary {...} braces in prose. Both the lookbehind and the lookahead are zero-width: the begin match itself is only the '{' character, so this rule can never consume, tag, or otherwise claim the backticks or the language word, which is what would risk breaking embedded-language/code-block highlighting for the whole block.
fence-meta-attributes.name: meta.directive.fence-meta.markii
